input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Let me explain it in a simple way:

Imagine you and your friends are playing a game together, but you’re all in different houses. How do you make sure everyone knows what’s happening at the same time? 

Online games like CoD or WoW are like a super-fast messenger. When you do something in the game (like move your character or shoot a gun), the game quickly sends that information to everyone else playing. It’s like the game is saying, “Hey, everyone! [Player’s name] just did this!” and it does it super fast—so fast that it feels like everyone is playing together in the same room, even if they’re not. 

The game uses the internet to zoom these messages to everyone, so you all stay in sync and can play together smoothly.
